NTA, JEE (Main) 2026 Session 2 final answer key of B.E./B.Tech on which result compiled, Exam Date 02.04.2026, Shift First (page 1)

notes: Previous-year questions from NTA's JEE (Main) 2026 paper of 2 April 2026, Shift 1 (B.E./B.Tech), ingested with pyq-ingest. Stems, options, statements and list items keep NTA's English wording exactly; NTA published this paper in English only, so the Hindi is our translation (hi_source: translation) and must be reviewed as such. Answers are NTA's final key (result-compiled, Session 2); our own solutions reach the same answer for every question in this file. Question ids 9001 and up mark ingested PYQs. Review before use: q.phy.ray-optics.spherical-refraction.9001 (paper Q41) needs its figure img.ray-optics.pyq-refracting-surface, which is requested, not approved; it is mock-only so it never ships in a device bundle without the figure.

stem.en: Refer the figure given below. $\mu_1$ and $\mu_2$ are refractive indices of air and lens material. The height of image will be ______ $\mathrm{cm}$.
stem.hi: नीचे दिए गए चित्र को देखिए। $\mu_1$ और $\mu_2$ क्रमशः वायु और लेंस पदार्थ के अपवर्तनांक हैं। प्रतिबिंब की ऊँचाई ______ $\mathrm{cm}$ होगी।

feynman.en: Use the single-surface formula $\frac{\mu_2}{v}-\frac{\mu_1}{u}=\frac{\mu_2-\mu_1}{R}$. The centre of curvature is on the incoming side, so $R$ is negative. Magnification is $\frac{\mu_1v}{\mu_2u}$.
feynman.hi: एकल सतह सूत्र $\frac{\mu_2}{v}-\frac{\mu_1}{u}=\frac{\mu_2-\mu_1}{R}$ का उपयोग कीजिए। वक्रता केंद्र आपतित प्रकाश की ओर है, अतः $R$ ऋणात्मक है। आवर्धन $\frac{\mu_1v}{\mu_2u}$ है।

steps.en: $m=\frac{\mu_1v}{\mu_2u}=\frac{29.6}{1.54 \times 40} \approx 0.48$, so the image height is $\approx 0.96\ \mathrm{cm}$, closest to $1\ \mathrm{cm}$.
steps.hi: $m=\frac{\mu_1v}{\mu_2u}=\frac{29.6}{1.54 \times 40} \approx 0.48$, अतः प्रतिबिंब की ऊँचाई $\approx 0.96\ \mathrm{cm}$ है, जो $1\ \mathrm{cm}$ के निकटतम है।
